**The held-out arm of the layer-0 node (iteration-9 correction).** The layer-0 MLP at the condition span has a held-out effect of exactly 0.00 nats under ablation and steering because the held-out edit was never applied. The class means that the edit writes are taken, for a condition-span node, only over pair prompts of the held-out prompt's own template (`MeanCache.get` in `src/k3circuit.py`, line 482: `if cl == "COND" and p["template"] != ref["template"]:`; line 485 also skips prompts whose span length differs). The 10 held-out prompts are templates F11 to F15 and the 20 pair prompts F1 to F10, so 0 of the 10 held-out prompts has a matching pair prompt, the mean is None (line 488), no edit is built, and the edited and unedited margins coincide; the stored rows show the node and all 50 matched random components of the same class at exactly 0 on every held-out prompt (20 of 20 prompt-by-mode rows). The node's 5.43 nats (ablation) and 4.94 nats (steering) over 30 prompts are therefore 8.14 and 7.41 nats over the 20 pair prompts plus ten zeros (8.14 x 20 / 30 = 5.43); the identity mean x 30 = pair mean x 20 + held-out mean x 10 holds for every node of both tables, and no other node has an exact-zero held-out effect (1 node in all, under both modes). Its held-out status is untested, not failed: on the descriptive natural contrast, whose held-out prompts share templates with its pairs, the same node gives 0.28 nats under ablation and 0.25 under steering on 5 held-out prompts (sign-flip p 0.031, the smallest one-sided p that five prompts allow, 1/32). BASE (B3) of iteration 9 reruns the held-out arm with template-matched means.

**Is 'opposite' a property of the names? (iteration-9 correction)** Each of the 300 forced prompts names its algorithm by one of three aliases, and the aliases of the edge algorithms share words with the banned names. On iteration 8's own stored geodesics at block 31 (every gate passes: the stored labels, prompt groups and algorithm-level g reproduce to 1e-9, and an independent kNN-geodesic recomputation from the stored states correlates with the stored k 15 matrix at 1.000), each non-banned algorithm was split into its three alias sets of 10 prompts and each set's g was computed (unit-weight Dijkstra 18.1 to 24.2, jump point search 14.2 to 18.8, IDA* 11.8 to 15.6, bidirectional A* 11.0 to 12.3, bidirectional BFS 9.2 to 12.4). The lexical overlap was committed by hash before any alias-level number: the number of banned-name detectors an alias matches (0 for every unit-weight Dijkstra and jump point search alias, 1 for every bidirectional BFS and bidirectional A* alias, 1 to 3 for IDA*). Across the 15 alias sets at k 15 the Spearman correlation is -0.61 (exact one-sided p 0.009 over all 360,360 assignments; 95% interval over template resamples -0.71 to -0.59), -0.77 at k 10 (p 0.0007), and -0.77 with content-word overlap. That statistic treats the 15 sets as exchangeable although they are nested in five algorithms, and between algorithms lexical overlap is confounded with mechanism: bidirectional BFS is next to BFS both in name and in mechanism. At the level of algorithms the correlation is -0.63 with p 0.13 (exact over 120 permutations; the tied overlap vector cannot go below 0.033). Holding the algorithm fixed and varying only the name, the within-algorithm test on content-word overlap (3 algorithms whose aliases differ; exact null over 216 distinct relabelings) gives a mean within-algorithm Spearman of -0.12 (p 0.46; p 0.72 at k 10), and the fixed-effects slope of g on overlap is 2.36 (two-sided stratified p 0.78), the wrong sign for a name effect. A sensitivity committed as optional scores overlap with the model's own BPE tokens (function words included, so every algorithm's aliases differ): the 15-set correlation is -0.77, and the within-algorithm statistic is -0.50 (p 0.057 over 7,776 relabelings; -0.40, p 0.11 at k 10), so a small within-algorithm name effect cannot be excluded at this resolution. Placebos fail as they must (at the 0.05 level, shuffled point labels reject in a share 0.048 of draws and random overlap vectors in 0.050) and a planted effect is recovered (rho -0.92, p 3e-06). By the committed wording rule: g follows alias overlap across algorithms (rho -0.61, exact p 0.009), but the pattern is carried by algorithm identity; on this manifold names and mechanisms are confounded, and TP-G's name-free manifolds decide. The planner's expectation of about -0.70 was public before the computation, so only the within-algorithm test and the interval were unseen; tables/alias_g.csv of the Step-0 artifact gives every set.

**The dial's geometry (iteration-9 correction).** Figure fig_gemma_dial_geometry plots Gemma's block-17 fork states in actual activation coordinates: the 120 twin variants (coloured by fork margin), the forced-BFS and forced-DFS sources, the free twin at its decision position, and the same free-twin states after the rank-4 DAS edit toward BFS or DFS and after the difference-in-means edit toward BFS. In the DAS plane the twin states form one tight cluster; the DAS edits carry them onto the forced-BFS or forced-DFS sources, while the difference-in-means edit throws them far beyond every natural state. In the twins' own first two principal components the DAS-edited states stay inside the twin columns and the difference-in-means states leave them. This is the retention picture of Table 406: a subspace that the twins' noun-driven variation barely uses but that prompts use, and an edit along it that stays near the natural states where the difference-in-means edit does not.
